* LOCATIONS AFFECTED
- Avery Island

- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind
- Peak Wind Forecast: 20-30 mph with gusts to 30 mph

to 57 mph
- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Plan for hazardous wind of equivalent tropical storm
force.
- PREPARE: Remaining efforts to protect property should be
completed as soon as possible. Prepare for limited wind
damage.
- ACT: Move to safe shelter before the wind becomes hazardous.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees
are shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown
over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within
urban or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving
conditions on bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* STORM SURGE
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Localized storm surge possible
- Peak Storm Surge Inundation: The potential for 1-3 feet
above ground somewhere within surge prone areas
- Window of concern: Begins this evening

areas.

farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.

overspread with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous

mainly in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.

* WHAT...River and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast New York, including the following
counties, Bronx and Westchester.

* WHEN...Until 715 AM EDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low lying
and flood prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 712 PM EDT, Gauge reports indicate rising water levels
from earlier heavy rain.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Bronx River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding. Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 20 at 3:54PM AKDT until July 22 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water could enter a few low-lying cabins along the Yentna River,
particularly near Lake Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 346 PM AKDT, the river gauge on the Yentna River indicates
rises in water levels from heavy rain across the advisory
area. Minor flooding is expected to continue or begin
shortly, especially along the Yentna River near Lake Creek.
- Anticipate water levels along the Yentna River to continue
rising before reaching a crest Tuesday afternoon. Water will
then slowly recede below minor flood levels by around
Wednesday night.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 2:50pm the stage was 20.9 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 22.0 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Tuesday.

Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Anglers Inn & King Point Lodges will have water
in several cabins.

At 22.0 feet: Several lodges and resorts will have water in a
number of cabins with water also encroaching the main lodge
buildings.


For Yentna River near Yentna Station:
At 3:59pm the stage was 18.1 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 21.6 feet is expected around 10:00pm
Tuesday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- If you live near or along Yentna River, stay alert and be
prepared to take action.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 20 at 3:45PM AKDT until July 22 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Skwentna River.

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 341 PM AKDT, the river gauge at Skwentna indicates rises
in water levels from heavy rain across the advisory area.
Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly,
especially near Skwentna River. Between 2.5 and 3.5 inches of
rain have fallen.
- For Skwentna River at Skwentna:
At 11:30am the stage was 40.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 42.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 43.3 feet is expected around 4:00am
Tuesday.

Impacts:
At 41.5 feet: Water starts to flow over low spots on the road
which is adjacent to an active slough.
At 43.5 feet: Water starts to encroach some houses located
near the active slough on the east side of town.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- If you live near or along the Skentna River stay alert and be
prepared to take action.

television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
